chapter: Hollywood, Ken Murray and the Penguin years
title: Penguin Records and Henry Dresnon
summary: Records for Penguin in 1945, run by his new manager, Henry Dresnon.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Would you have gotten Willard Brown back again?
I did get Willard Brown back. Bob Carroll was back with me.
Where's Rickman, Rickman was with you around the time that you were recording for this Penguin label.
No, you recorded before '48. '45 you made records for--
All right; this is '45, here's Fauntleroy, here's Abie Baker, this is Kenny Rickman, "Buji" Ward, George "Buji" Ward--I don't know this guy.
He wasn't working with you, was he?
Something happened to the piano player and we got Arnie Hollup. He was a good man.
How did the contract with Penguin come up, did you get it or was it Billy Shaw?
That was--at that time my manager owned Penguin; I had a new manager.
Those were the first records you made since Decca.
Oh, after Penguin. That would have been around '47?
I made a bunch of them. I got a tape of them in there now. Here's a write up from Walter Winchell's column.
